title: Ozone and warmth gave no clear repeated link to next-year US bird survey coverage in 1995-2023
abstract: We tested whether seasonal ozone changed the link between warmth and next-year bird survey coverage. We used a verified published panel from the US Breeding Bird Survey, EPA and NOAA. Four East and West, early and late models used 31,586 accepted current surveys. Interaction estimates ranged from -1.05 to +1.13 percentage points per 10 ppb ozone and 2 C warmth. All four corrected intervals included zero. The pooled estimate from 31,741 surveys was +0.18, with a 95% interval of -0.65 to +1.02. Observer controls and current bird-count controls did not give a clear pooled interaction. Coverage means that the source panel contains an accepted record in the next calendar year. It does not identify why a survey is absent. Selected routes, missing exposures, coarse weather, and limited western state clusters restrict inference. This test does not establish absence of observation bias or a causal effect on birds. The package includes new code, aggregate results, a figure, exact input hashes and an external-data retrieval program.

display.caption: The ozone by warmth slope for next-year accepted panel coverage. Four split intervals have a four-test correction. Pooled intervals are 95%.

citations.reason: We use its verified panel to build a new next-year coverage outcome. Biological records overlap.
